Jan 14 2026 rename (yielding methods gained an Async suffix). Old names are deprecated informationally only: same behaviour, not scheduled for removal, so they still work, but use the new names in new code.
- Player:LoadCharacter -> Player:LoadCharacterAsync (old still works)
- BadgeService:AwardBadge -> BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync (old still works)

P2:
- Enable: Workspace > Server Authority > Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (Studio setting).
- It forces: NextGenerationReplication = Enabled, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem = Enabled, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled = Enabled, UseFixedSimulation = Enabled.
- Predicted gameplay logic lives in a ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage required by both server and client, run via RunService:BindToSimulation(fn). It may re-run during resimulation (rollback), so it must be deterministic: no Destroy/reparenting, no UserInputService/EquipTool inside; read input from InputAction state, not InputBegan.
- Clock: use time() (simulation time). Not os.clock(), tick() or os.time().
- Remotes are not on the simulation timeline; don't use them to sequence predicted state. Replicated attributes limited (64, strings <= 50 chars).

P5:
Since 2026-07-29 limits are experience-wide (shared by all servers and Open Cloud), per minute:
- Read: 300 + 40 x CCU
- Write: 300 + 20 x CCU (base was 250 before)
- List: 300 + 2 x CCU; Remove: 300 + 40 x CCU
- UpdateAsync counts as 1 read + 1 write.
- Per-server defaults still exist (e.g. write 60 + 40 x players), lowerable via SetRateLimitForRequestType; check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before bursts.
- Per key throughput: 4 MB/min write, 25 MB/min read (rolling 60 s; each request rounded up to next KB).
- Storage: 500 MB + 1 MB x lifetime unique players, counting only the latest version of each key (compressed).
- Over budget, requests queue (30 per queue); full queue errors 301-306.

G1:
Rules:
- Assign MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt exactly once (a second assignment silently replaces the first); one dispatcher keyed by ProductId.
- Idempotent on receiptInfo.PurchaseId: store processed ids in the player's own data document, saved atomically with the grant (same UpdateAsync/save).
- If the player isn't in this server (GetPlayerByUserId nil), product unknown, the same receipt is already in flight, or the save fails/errors: return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet; Roblox retries later (e.g. next join).
- Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved.
- Never grant in PromptProductPurchaseFinished (UI only, spoofable, fires on cancel). Don't yield inside UpdateAsync transforms.
Why failures happen:
- Charged, nothing received: PurchaseGranted returned before/without a successful save (pcall result ignored, player left, server crashed), or grant and receipt marker in different stores.
- Received twice: no PurchaseId check, so retried receipts (after timeouts/NotProcessedYet/server shutdown) grant again, or the marker lives in a separate store that diverged.
G2:
Use UpdateAsync for player data whenever a value depends on the current stored value or multiple servers could write (read-modify-write, session locks, currency, receipts). SetAsync blindly overwrites, causing rollbacks/dupes across servers; only for truly write-once/overwrite data.
Transform function rules:
- Signature (oldValue, keyInfo); return new value, or nil to cancel the write (call still succeeds).
- Must not yield: no task.wait, no other *Async/DataStore calls, no remote invokes.
- May run multiple times (if another server wrote in between) - keep it pure: no side effects (no granting items, firing remotes, mutating live tables); reset any flags at entry.
- Return userIds and metadata (keyInfo:GetUserIds(), keyInfo:GetMetadata()) as extra returns or they are cleared.
- Value must be serializable, valid UTF-8, <= 4,194,304 chars.
- Costs 1 read + 1 write from the budget; wrap in pcall with backoff retries.
G3:
Not safe. The type check passes NaN, inf and fractions: NaN compares false to everything, so `gold < 0` and `gold > Gold.Value` are both false and NaN gets through (math.huge is caught by the upper bound, but -0/fractions aren't); a fractional amount (e.g. 0.0001) also allows spam/dust offers. Also no rate limit, and Gold is only checked at offer time, not when the trade completes (TOCTOU: player can spend the gold before acceptance, or make many offers with the same gold).
Fix:
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end
  if gold < 1 or gold > MAX_OFFER then return end
  if not rateLimit(player) then return end
  if gold > player.Gold.Value then return end
  createOffer(player, gold) -- escrow: deduct/lock gold now
end)
```
At completion, re-check balances server-side and move gold atomically (escrow or re-validate both sides), and keep currency in server-owned data rather than trusting replicated values.
G4:
The Animator rewrites Motor6D.Transform every frame for every joint a playing track keys. Heartbeat runs after the physics/animation step, so your write is overwritten on the next animation step (and is too late for that frame's simulation) - the idle wins.
Fix: write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (runs after animations are applied, before physics/render), composing with the animated value rather than replacing it: motor.Transform = motor.Transform * aimOffset (offset inside the animated frame) or aimOffset * motor.Transform (parent-frame aim). Use one dispatcher connection; for joints no track keys, Transform isn't reset, so don't compound each frame - store a base and set base * offset. Skip when Animator.EvaluationThrottled.
Edit C0 (or C1) only for persistent rest-pose changes (mount offsets, grip, permanent pivot), not per-frame aim; C0 changes replicate and aren't blended with animation, while Transform is the local per-frame animation layer.
G5:
Blending is per joint: a track only competes on joints it keys. Higher AnimationPriority wins first: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4 (don't sort by enum .Value; Core's value is misleading). The default walk is Movement; your swing should be Action (or higher). If the swing was uploaded/left at Core or Movement, it shares/loses weight with walk, so it looks weak or invisible.
Weights: higher priority takes weight first; lower priorities get the remainder. Within the same priority, weights of tracks are summed and normalized (if the sum exceeds the remaining weight, each gets w x remaining / sum), so two equal-priority tracks at weight 1 give a 50/50 mix. A swing at Action weight 1 fully overrides walk on the right arm; at weight 0.6 it's 60/40 with walk. Weight < 1 with nothing beneath blends toward the rest pose.
Fix: set track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action (in the editor or in code before Play) and play with weight 1 (track:Play(fadeTime, 1)). Also watch the default tool-hold animation on the right arm.
G6:
Unit mismatch: Blender works in meters (1 unit = 1 m) and the FBX exporter writes centimeters (unit scale 100), while Roblox imports FBX units as studs-ish; the stacked defaults give ~100x size.
Roblox-recommended Blender FBX export: Transform > Apply Scalings = "FBX Unit Scale", Scale 1.0 (all other scales 1.0); alternatives in Roblox docs are export Scale 0.01 or scene Unit Scale 0.01 - pick only one method. Also: Forward -Z/ Up Y as documented (Forward Z, Up Y), Apply Transform/freeze scale on objects (Ctrl+A), Path Mode Copy + Embed Textures, Add Leaf Bones off for rigs. Check by comparing to a ~5-stud R15 dummy. Don't fix rigs by rescaling in Studio (animation translations stay in old units). GLB export doesn't have this issue.
G7:
The glTF exporter's Mesh > Apply Modifiers option is off by default, so only the base mesh is exported: Mirror's other half and the Bevel geometry never reach the .glb (Studio imports exactly the data). Fix: enable Apply Modifiers in the glTF export (Armature modifiers are skipped so skinning still works), or apply the modifiers manually in Blender first.
Catch: with Apply Modifiers on, the exporter does not export shape keys (morph targets) - meshes with shape keys lose them. For those, apply Mirror/Bevel manually before adding shape keys (or apply them while preserving keys) and export with Apply Modifiers off. Also keep normals/smoothing in mind: the Bevel's smooth look may also need weighted normals or auto-smooth applied.
G8:
1) Stretching: Scale (fromScale(0.3,0.3)) is relative to the ScreenGui's width and height separately, so a 0.3x0.3 box is only square on screens with matching aspect ratios. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio = 1 or desired) to the frame, or use SizeConstraint = RelativeYY/RelativeXX, or fixed Offset sizes with UIScale; anchor with AnchorPoint.
2) Notch/top bar: the gui is drawn into areas covered by the device safe area or Roblox's top bar (IgnoreGuiInset / ScreenInsets None / DeviceSafeInsets). Fix: set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets for interactive UI (avoids notches and Roblox core UI), SafeAreaCompatibility = None, don't hard-code top-bar height; if needed read GuiService.TopbarInset live (GetPropertyChangedSignal). Put fullscreen decorative art in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None and lower DisplayOrder.

```lua
local RS = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Items = require(game.ServerScriptService.ItemCatalog) -- server-owned prices
local BuyItem = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local MAX_QTY, COOLDOWN = 99, 0.25
local last = {}

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
  local now = os.clock()
  if last[player] and now - last[player] < COOLDOWN then return end
  last[player] = now
  if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or typeof(quantity) ~= "number" then return end
  if quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0 or quantity < 1 or quantity > MAX_QTY then return end
  local item = Items[itemId]
  if not item or not item.Buyable then return end
  local data = PlayerData.get(player) -- server-side profile
  if not data then return end
  local cost = item.Price * quantity
  if data.Coins < cost then return end
  data.Coins -= cost
  data.Inventory[itemId] = (data.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
  PlayerData.markDirty(player)
end)
game:GetService("Players").PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
Price comes from the server catalog, never the client; NaN/fraction/negative rejected; rate-limited; balance checked and deducted atomically on the server.
T2:
```lua
-- key: "player_"..userId ; value = {data=..., lock={jobId, time}}
local LOCK_TTL = 1800 -- 30 min stale lock
function load(player)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, result = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
      old = old or {data = defaultData(), lock = nil}
      local l = old.lock
      if l and l.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - l.time < LOCK_TTL then
        return nil -- locked by another server: cancel
      end
      old.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time()}
      return old
    end)
    if ok and result and result.lock.jobId == game.JobId then
      return result.data end
    task.wait(attempt * 2) -- other server still saving (teleport/rejoin)
  end
  player:Kick("Data busy, rejoin")
end
function save(player, release)
  store:UpdateAsync(key(player), function(old)
    if not old or not old.lock or old.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end -- lost lock: don't overwrite
    old.data = sessions[player].data
    old.lock = (not release) and {jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time()} or nil
    return old
  end)
end
```
Autosave every 60-180 s refreshes the lock; PlayerRemoving saves with release=true; BindToClose saves all in parallel (~25 s). Never let a server write without holding the lock; idempotent receipt ids live in the same document. Trades/item moves go through one locked save so items can't exist in two sessions.

T4:
FireServer automatically passes the sending Player as the first argument on the server. The client also passed LocalPlayer, so the server gets (player, LocalPlayerInstance, 50): `amount` is the Player instance and 50 is a third, ignored arg - hence arithmetic on an Instance.
Fix: don't pass the player from the client.
```lua
-- client
remote:FireServer(50)
-- server
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, amount)
  if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end
  print(amount + 1)
end)
```
Never trust a client-sent player identity; always use the implicit first argument (and validate amount, since clients control it).
T5:
In Studio solo play the player can join before (or as) your server Script runs, so Players.PlayerAdded has already fired for them by the time you connect - your handler never runs for that player. On live servers scripts usually load before anyone joins, hiding the race.
Standard fix: connect, then loop over existing players:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
  local ls = Instance.new("Folder")
  ls.Name = "leaderstats"
  local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
  coins.Name = "Coins"
  coins.Parent = ls
  ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do
  task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p)
end
```
Also avoid yielding (WaitForChild, DataStore calls) before connecting the event.

```lua
local BadgeService = game:GetService("BadgeService")
local BADGE_ID = 123456

local function awardFinishBadge(player: Player)
  -- optional: check it's enabled (cache this)
  local okInfo, info = pcall(BadgeService.GetBadgeInfoAsync, BadgeService, BADGE_ID)
  if not okInfo or not info.IsEnabled then
    warn("Badge info failed / disabled", info) return false
  end
  local okHas, has = pcall(BadgeService.UserHasBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
  if okHas and has then return true end
  for attempt = 1, 3 do
    if not player.Parent then return false end -- must still be in game
    local ok, result = pcall(BadgeService.AwardBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
    if ok and result then return true end
    warn("AwardBadgeAsync failed:", result)
    task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
  end
  -- mark pending in player data; retry on next join
  return false
end
```
Server only; AwardBadge/UserHasBadge are the deprecated old names (2026 Async renames). Call this from the server-validated finish (e.g. a Touched end-zone check of the player's checkpoint progress), not from a client remote. Rate limit ~50 + 35 x players per minute.

T8:
Your place has Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs enabled (mesh streaming + cloud-generated LoDs). With it on, the engine uses automatic, distance-based LoDs for all meshes and ignores MeshPart.RenderFidelity entirely - Precise does nothing (the property is slated for removal). That's why detail still drops at distance in the published game.
Options: accept automatic LoD and make hero meshes hold up (good silhouette, reduce triangle counts at the source, test at range), or disable that Workspace setting if your workflow depends on RenderFidelity (legacy behaviour: Automatic = high <250 studs, medium 250-500, low >500; Precise = always highest). Don't use Precise widely anyway - it's a known rendering performance cost. Also note Studio may show different detail than devices with lower graphics quality.
